title: Big discoveries begin with small questions
excerpt: A simple ‘why?’ can open the door to a whole new way of seeing the world.
paragraphs: Curiosity often starts with something ordinary: a shadow on the floor, a seed in a pot, or a pattern in a favourite story. Giving children time to notice and wonder makes these everyday moments part of learning.

Try exploring one question together instead of rushing to an answer. Ask what your child thinks might happen, make a simple observation, and talk about what surprised you. Drawing or writing down the discovery can help keep the conversation going.
The aim is to make asking questions feel welcome. A thoughtful question is already a valuable step towards understanding.

title: Make a little room for reading together
excerpt: Small, unhurried moments with a book can become a lovely family ritual.
paragraphs: Reading together does not have to look the same every day. Some days it might be a chapter; other days, a favourite page or a conversation about an illustration is enough.
Let your child choose a story and take turns noticing details. Ask which character they would like to meet or what they imagine happens after the final page. Leave space for their own interpretation.
Keep the routine comfortable and flexible. The shared attention and enjoyment are as much a part of the experience as the words on the page.

title: A blank page, a hundred possibilities
excerpt: Making room for imagination through colour, texture, and a little experimentation.
paragraphs: A creative afternoon can begin with paper, pencils, and a few materials already at home. Children can invent a place, illustrate a story, or build something from clean packaging.
Instead of choosing how the finished piece should look, invite your child to explain their ideas. Questions such as ‘What would you like to try next?’ give them room to make decisions and experiment.
Enjoy the process together. An unexpected colour or a structure that needs rebuilding can become the beginning of a new idea.

title: Learning to cheer for each other
excerpt: The small moments of encouragement that make being part of a team meaningful.
paragraphs: Being part of a team includes many small choices: listening to an idea, taking turns, welcoming someone new, and noticing another person’s effort.
Games and group activities offer opportunities to practise these choices. After an activity, talk about a moment when someone helped, encouraged, or made space for another participant.
Celebrating these moments alongside the result helps make participation feel worthwhile for everyone.
